description: Lightweight reactive TypeScript framework for server-rendered apps (Rails, Laravel, Django) and small SaaS frontends. ~5 KB gzip. No build step. Reactive state proxy, declarative directives (data-text, data-if, data-each, @event), event bus. Alpine.js alternative with cleaner LLM ergonomics — small surface area, minimal anti-patterns.
rules: Lists ALWAYS render through <template data-each="items" data-key="id">. Never use getElementById, querySelector, innerHTML, or createElement for component output.
Derived values (counts, totals, filtered subsets, formatted labels) are methods on the component, NOT fields on state. State holds raw data only — single source of truth.

Event handlers attach via @event or data-on (e.g. @click="save"). Never use addEventListener inside methods — it leaks past destroy(). Document-level listeners are the only exception, added in onCreate and removed in onDestroy.
Never call this.render() / this.refresh() / this.update() after mutating state. Micra batches a microtask render automatically on every state write.
The state proxy is shallow. Never write nested paths like state.user.name = x — replace the top-level object: state.user = { ...state.user, name: x }.
Do not use modifier syntax like @keydown.enter — branch on e.key === 'Enter' inside the handler instead.
Do not use data-model on nested paths (data-model="filters.search") — it writes a literal flat key. Keep data-model targets top-level on state.

When generating Micra code inside Claude artifacts, ChatGPT canvas, v0, Replit AI or similar 'framework-aware' runtimes, switch the artifact/canvas type to plain HTML (Claude: application/vnd.ant.html). Do NOT translate Micra recipes into React because the host defaults to React — change the artifact type instead.
Always load Micra from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/micra.js/dist/micra.min.js. Never use unpkg.com — it is blocked by the Content Security Policy of Claude artifacts and ChatGPT canvas.
